subject: Analytic maritime sky, solar disc and atmosphere-aware lighting
identity: A clean blue zenith transitions into a bright aerosol horizon without a hard colour band.
The sun remains a compact disc with a restrained forward-scattering halo rather than a nearby sphere.
Low sun warms the direct light, haze, clouds and ocean reflection together.
Cloud and fog presets change aerosol density without breaking the shared sun direction.
invariants: Sky scattering, directional light, sun sprites and ocean reflection share one sun direction.
The solar angular radius is 0.004675 radians and the disc is positioned behind scene geometry.
The sky owns tone-mapped radiance while the display-referred solar sprites own no bloom dependency.
Atmosphere gradients include low-amplitude display dithering to resist visible banding.
Weather transitions are damped and deterministic cloud placement uses a fixed seed.
One Three.js world unit remains one metre for scene and fog scale.
allowedDivergences: The sailing camera remains near sea level, so a lightweight analytic Preetham atmosphere is used instead of an orbital LUT stack.
A depth-aware aerial-perspective post pass is deferred; the bounded scene uses shared horizon-coloured exponential fog.
No lens-flare or bloom pass is required for sun readability.
